extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate creative writing students and instructors (MIT Genre Fiction Workshop)
extracted.subtask_description: An undergraduate workshop course focused on understanding and producing genre fiction, emphasizing the relationship between reader expectations and writer choices, awareness of subgenres, and cross-genre experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader-Writer Contact
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reader-Writer Contact that is at the heart of genre writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the agreement between what the reader wants and what the writer provides; consider how a writer establishes, fulfills, negotiates, or subverts the expectations implied by this contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres meet specific reader expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some critics say that different genres meet specific expectations of readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or producing genre fiction, assess how well the work aligns with the expectations associated with its genre(s). Consider whether genre functions merely as marketing or as a meaningful contract with readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgenre recognition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: We will look at how genres are divided into subgenres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the subgenre(s) at work and their particular conventions; evaluate how the piece adheres to, modifies, or challenges subgenre-specific norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-genre combination
rubrics_metrics.description: How genres are combined into cross-genre work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess techniques and effects of blending genres — how combination affects tone, plot, character expectations, and reader reception; evaluate coherence and intentionality of the blend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre innovation through crossing genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Crossing genres has led to the establishment of new genres (steampunk, preternatural romance) and strongly established subgenres (historical mystery, urban fantasy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider historical and creative outcomes of genre-mixing: does crossing genres produce a convincing new form or merely dilute expectations? Evaluate originality, internal logic, and whether the hybrid yields a sustainable genre or subgenre.
